- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., post-75+ levels), then underestimates the subsequent decline.
- Underestimates mean-reverting lows (e.g., 68–70 range) and fails to recognize downward momentum.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and too pessimistic in the medium term (7–15 days).
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing true price reversals — often misses early signs of correction.
- Overconfidence in recent high prices leads to persistent overforecasting of future highs.
- When history shows strong downward momentum, model fails to adjust downward quickly enough.
- Forecasts are less accurate when true outcomes are clustered near the 70–73 range — model overfits to recent volatility.
